see.b: Completed in September 1926, the Aloha Tower was for a long time the tallest building in Honolulu and was the first thing that tourists arriving by ship would see.

see.h: Mon–Sat 10AM–4PM; closed all State and Federal holidays
see.b: Occupies the second floor of a beautifully restored historic building with displays of visual art by Hawaii artists in three galleries with both permanent and rotating displays. Also has evening concerts on the lawn.
Seat of the Episcopal Diocese of Hawaii. Commissioned by King Kamehameha IV and Queen Emma and completed by King Kamehameha V in 1867.

The Westminster Abbey of Hawaii, historic church of Hawaiian royalty, constructed between 1836 and 1842 from coral rock. King Lunalias tomb is on the grounds and there is a historic cemetery adjacent to the church.

see.n: Cathedral of Our Lady of Peace
see.b: Seat of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Honolulu, the original structure dates to 1843.

see.n: Hawaiian Mission Houses Historic Site and Archives
see.b: Three restored houses, temporary exhibition gallery, and research library provide a unique glimpse into 19th-century Hawaiian life. The houses are only accessible by guided tour Tu F Sa at 11AM and 1PM, and Sa 3PM.
A collection of rare and beautiful plants from the tropical regions of the world. Docent-led tours everyday at 10:30AM.

Completed in 1969, the State Capitol has a modern, open-air design, with pillars reminiscent of palm tree trunks, and two conical structures symbolizing volcanoes containing the House and Senate chambers, all surrounded by a moat of…

Iolani Palace dates back to 1882 and was the official residence of the Hawaiian Kingdom's last two monarchs. As a result of careful restoration and continued preservation, today's visitors to this National Historic Landmark in downtown…
A historic building that is the seat of the Hawaii State Supreme Court and is noted for the Kamehameha the Great Statue in front, which is often adorned with leis.

see.n: King Kamehameha V Judiciary History Center
see.b: A small history museum about the judicial process and Hawaii’s legal history.
The private home of Hawaii's last monarch, Queen Liliuokalani, it is now the governor's mansion. Call to reserve tours.
In the Hawaiian language, "Honolulu Hale" literally means "Honolulu House", a fitting name for Honolulu's city hall.

A pleasant green space with plenty of grassy lawns and trees, as well as a lovely beach that's popular with local families. An outer reef keeps the water very calm, perfect for children or a nice swim. Lifeguards, showers, restrooms,…
Boat charters are available from Kewalo Basin, adjacent to Ala Moana Park, with numerous operators offering short cruises.

A nice park southeast of Downtown, situated on the water. There's no beach, but a pleasant oceanside walk and some rolling, grassy hills. Just off-shore is a popular surfing spot known as "Point Panic".

One of the defining landmarks of Hawaii is this ancient volcanic crater which dominates over the surrounding area. An observation deck at the top offers breathtaking views of the southern coast of Oahu. After entering the monument…

Another popular roadside stop, the Halona Blowhole is one of many blowholes (ocean caves with a hole in the top, so water shoots out the top) along the coast, although this one is easy to view, located right under a parking lot, and can…

A 200-acre botanical garden located inside a volcanic crater, with many rare dry climate plants such as African plants, cacti and succulents, plumeria, native wiliwili, dry land palms and bougainvillea.

Another popular roadside stop west of the Halona Blowhole, the Lana'i Lookout is located on a piece of land that juts out into the ocean. There is a parking lot and many people take pictures of the open ocean crashing onto the rocks. It…

At Makapu'u Point, the very southeastern corner of the island, this roadside stop offers scenic views of Makapu'u Point and up the windward coast of Oahu. The 1.75 mile Makapu'u Point trail leads from the parking lot to the historic…
A Sea World-esque theme park with marine animal shows and an aquarium. For a small fortune, you can also swim with dolphins or sea lions.

see.h: Summer: Wed-Mon 6AM-7PM. Winter: Wed-Mon 6AM-6PM. Closed Tuesdays
see.pr: $7.50 adults, Hawaii residents and children under 13 free; parking $1/vehicle
see.b: Hanauma Bay is not a place for beach sports but is instead a bay formed in the crater of an extinct volcano and filled with a wonderful coral reef and many fish. The calm waters and abundance of marine life make it an excellent place…

Known as "the Peering Place", this is a small, rocky cove with a small sandy beach that is great for swimming when the surf is calm. It requires a small hike down to the beach, and there's no lifeguard or facilities, so it's swim at…

A very scenic, rocky beach that's usually too rough for swimming but is a very popular spot for surfing and bodysurfing. During the summer the beach is wide and the ocean is usually calm, but during the winter high surf erodes the…

True to its name, this is a nice, wide stretch of beach that's great for swimming when the surf is calm. When the water is rough though, the shorebreak and rip tide currents create steep, hard-breaking waves that make it rather…

A 7.5 acre public city park, portions of which were a garden that belonged to Queen Liliuokalani, the last reigning Monarch of Hawaii. This is the only one of the five botanical gardens that contain only plants native to Hawaii.

This museum, founded in 1927 by Anna Rice Cooke, encompasses 32 galleries surrounding six courtyard gardens and houses one of the largest collections of Asian art in the United States, with an impressive Western collection to boot,…

see.n: The National Memorial Cemetery of the Pacific
see.b: Situated in the middle of Punchbowl, an extinct crater, this is the final resting place for over 38,000 personnel from WWII, the Korean War and Vietnam. A shrine also commemorates the missing-in-action. It's also the resting place of…

In the Nu'uanu valley is this restored historic building, built in 1847 as the summer retreat of Queen Emma, wife of King Kamehameha IV. Self-guided and docent-led tours of the palace are available and offer a glimpse into the lifestyle…
A massive botanical garden at the top of Manoa that's run by the University of Hawai'i with a wide variety of tropical plants as well as scenic waterfalls and views of Manoa.
A 1.5 miles hike to a very tall waterfall. Parking is available a little bit before the trailhead.

see.h: Apr 1-Labor Day: Daily 7AM-7:45PM; Labor Day-Apr 1: Daily 7AM-6:45PM
see.b: One of the more popular scenic vistas on O'ahu and the site of one of the bloodiest battles in Hawaiian history, the Pali Lookout provides a panoramic view of Windward O'ahu. Also interesting at this site is the Old Pali Road, formerly…

Above Makiki, this park provides a stunning view of southern O'ahu which includes Diamond Head, Waikiki, downtown Honolulu, Punch Bowl Crater and the airport. There are also hiking trails which allow you to completely forget that you…

Lovely zoo with lots of exotic animals and plenty of the big-name ones like elephants, rhinos, lions, zebras and giraffes. Parking is $1.50/hour, but free parking is available at the Waikiki Shell across the street.

The third oldest aquarium in the US, has many of species of marine life from Hawaii and the Pacific, including sharks, octopus, jellyfish, colorful reef fish, and coral. The outdoor exhibit of Hawaiian monk seals is temporarily closed.…
Named after legendary surfer Duke Kahanamoku, this is a man-made beach and lagoon on the Ala Moana end of Waikiki, in front of the Hilton Hawaiian Village Resort.
Located adjacent to a park, this is the widest stretch of beach and one of the most popular. It is also a good spot for snorkeling, with a coral reef a little offshore.
This is perhaps the most crowded stretch of beach in Waikiki.

With an offshore retaining wall, this is a calmer section of beach that's great for families and beginner surfers. Along Kalakaua Avenue are four stones known as the Ancient Pohaku (Wizard Stones) which are believed to hold spiritual…
This is a quieter section of beach that's also popular with gays. The snorkeling is great here, with huge tangs, Moorish Idols and other fish.
This is a much quieter section of beach that's protected by a reef; great for families and swimming.
Submarine tours off the coast of Waikiki, getting up-close to marine life, coral reefs, and shipwrecks.

Founded in 1889 by Charles Reed Bishop, the last direct descendant of Kamehameha I, this massive museum is by far the largest in Hawaii, with a complex of buildings holding an excellent collection of artifacts from the islands. The main…

see.h: Closed temporarily, was daily 7:30AM-30min prior to sunset
see.b: A scenic public park is the Moanalua neighborhood, home to a small cottage which was home to Prince Lot Kamehameha (who would later become Kamehameha V) and a large monkeypod tree known as the "Hitachi Tree".

see.a: At Kamehameha Hwy (Hawaii 99) and Kalaoa St
see.h: Visitor center: Daily 7AM-5PM; closed Thanksgiving, 25 Dec, 1 Jan
see.pr: Free to enter, but $7-10 mandatory bag check
see.b: Well known for 7 December 1941, the "day that lived in infamy", when a surprise attack by Japanese forces killed over 2,000 U.S. military personnel and brought the U.S. into World War II. Today the harbor, still functioning as a navy…

This memorial, built over the hull of the sunken battleship USS Arizona, commemorates the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor which brought the U.S. into World War II. It also serves as the final resting place for many of the 1,177 who died…

A WWII-era submarine that is open for tours, giving you a look at a life aboard a submarine. A museum attached to the submarine has artifacts from the submarine. Enter through the USS Arizona entrance.

see.h: Sept-May: 8AM-4PM; Jun-Aug: 8AM-5PM; closed Thanksgiving, Dec 25, and Jan 1; ticket window closes 1 hour early
see.b: A perfect companion to the USS Arizona Memorial, this battleship is best known as the site where World War II ended when the Japanese military surrendered to the Allied forces. Tickets may be purchased at the USS Bowfin Museum. Visitors…

see.b: A large hanger full of military aircraft from WWII, with both authentic American and Japanese aircraft.

see.a: at Salt Lake Blvd and Kamehameha Hwy
see.b: Before its closure in 2020 due to structural issues, it was home to the University of Hawaii football team and the annual NCAA football Hawaii Bowl every December. (Both the team and bowl game have been moved to the UH campus for the…

An ice rink is probably the last thing you'd expect to find in a tropical city, but at least it makes for the perfect getaway if the hot climate is too much for you. If you don't own a pair of skates, there is a skate rental desk…

Tucked away behind an industrial area facing the Honolulu Harbor, this large park offers plenty of green lawns, excellent views of Downtown, and a very calm sandy beach that's never crowded and with fairly good swimming. No lifeguards;…

eat.b: Waterfront views of Waikiki Beach and Diamond Head. Seafood, steak, pasta.
A Japanese-style chain eatery, with employees shouting "irrashaimase!" (welcome) when you enter. Very popular with the younger people, offering many types of sushi moving on a rotating track.

Best dim sum in Honolulu, easily rivaling places in San Francisco, Los Angeles, etc. Located in Chinatown in a two level Chinese outdoor shopping plaza, Legend serves amazing and authentic dim sum at reasonable prices. Very popular with…

The island equivalent of Denny's, though far more popular with the locals. There's a wide variety of food, including plate lunches at reasonable prices; their signature dish is their chili, which they prepare in many different ways:…

eat.a: Ala Moana Shopping Center, Upper Level 4
eat.b: Popular among locals, especially on weekends and Wednesday nights. Live local music is played M-F 4-7PM, Sa Su 1PM-4PM, and nightly 9:30PM-12:30AM. Happy Hour 8PM-11PM.

Pub food and local specialties. Mr. Murphy reputedly hand-selects the corned beef, which should tell you something about the quality of the food (it's awesome!); they also pour an excellent pint of Guinness.

First opened in 1935 when this section of Chinatown was a red-light district and playground for merchant seamen. Come for the affordable drinks and friendly service. Stay for the ukulele jams and karaoke. There is always something to…
Large brewery and restaurant.

eat.h: Mon-Thu noon-10PM, Fri noon-11PM, Sat 10AM-11PM, Sun 10PM-10PM
eat.b: Brewery and beer garden.
Fine restaurant lauded for its contemporary island cuisine. Recommended are the pan-seared Hudson Valley foie gras, sashimi and slow-braised pork belly.
This funky little Japanese fusion joint is one of the best kept secrets in town. Be sure to try the garlic ahi. There can be a long line of locals on some nights. It's BYOB!

A very well known Mediterranean and Greek food spot among Honolulu resident's, this is a charming place, with most of its tables outside a small lanai. It is BYOB, and you can bring your own glasses to avoid the cup fee. There is a wine…

Easily the best place to get Hawaiian food in the islands -- popular with kama'aina and the savvy traveler willing to venture beyond the tourist track. Get the combination plate for a sampling of both kalua pig and lau lau (with some…

Known as the "Wolfgang Puck of the Pacific," Roy Yamaguchi specializes in Hawaiian fusion cuisine. This is the flagship restaurant of the Roy's Restaurant chain and overlooks Maunalua Bay with a lovely westward view.

As good and as cheap that an amazing delicious Thai meal can get. The place started as a Thai market, but has grown as a local favorite. The high quality of the food, associated with fresh ingredients and low prices make this spot a…

While there are many Thai restaurants on Oahu, this is one of the best and most reasonably priced. The Panang Curry is especially good. You have to drive or take a cab if you're staying in Waikiki, but it's well worth it!
Basic, decent Korean food at a budget price.

eat.a: Honolulu Museum of Art, 900 South Beretania St
eat.b: Situated in an indoor/outdoor setting, it's usually packed with locals. It's the place to go for imaginative salads and sandwiches at a reasonable price. The art isn't bad either.
Owned and operated by a Japanese couple. They offer high grade take-out sushi at budget prices. You can enjoy lunch or dinner here for well under $10.
One of the best places to get shave ice (local equivalent to snow cones). Popular with both locals and visitors. Very long lines during the summer heat, extremely limited parking, but still worth it.

This is one branch of a small chain. The name represents truth in advertising. The burgers are very big and juicy, and so are the grilled chicken breasts. The other ingredients, such as the lettuce, tomatoes, and onions are also fresh.…

Cafeteria-style restaurant specializing in Japanese Udon--thick, long noodles served with meat, vegetables and broth. There is usually a line out the door, but it is quick because it is cafeteria service.

eat.pr: Around $10 for a medium poke bowl
eat.b: Serves good poke bowls for a reasonable price. Lines can get long-ish around dinner time.
Named after legendary surfer Duke Kahanamoku. For meals and drinks right on the beach you can't beat Duke's. It's a bar and a restaurant. Their Sunday live music is a local favorite.

This very popular breakfast/brunch spot attracts lines, so don't go if you're in a big rush. They make excellent omelettes and pancakes, and there are three syrups on the table; the coconut syrup is the best of the three. Portions are…
This is an enclosed, but open-air sports bar on across the street from the beach.

Very informal, with colorful testimonials in various languages papering the walls. Clientele is primarily Korean, and staff speak little English, so don't expect a lot of help in deciding what to order. Just get whatever seems good to…
Good food and service.

The oldest and best-known gay-friendly nightspot showcasing a glassed in dance floor. Excellent cocktails, especially mai tais. Music videos are shown on big screens, and are all by request on Monday nights. Open to the air.
Daily happy hour from 2-5PM and 8PM-close.
Energetic pub atmosphere with live music playing every night.

Not only does it have a wonderful food menu, but they offer over 130 draft beers from all over the world, the huge island bar protects the 4 walls of taps within. If you were wondering how they can have so many beers on tap, just take a…

Serving freshly-prepared local food in the plate lunch style, Helena's is known for their Korean-style short ribs (galbi) and their lau lau. They tend to fill during mealtimes, and parking is scarce, so arriving just after the lunch…
Not much to speak of in terms of food or drink (their Mai Tai is alright) but the decor is straight out of a tiki-lovers paradise.
